title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a response to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its perspective and intended measures to tackle the concerns raised. It emphasizes commitments to enhance transparency, accountability, and public trust in AI while calling for continued research and regulatory progress.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: The EU Regulation 2024/1689 sets out harmonised rules for the use of artificial intelligence across the Union, establishing common standards and obligations for developers and users. It amends existing regulations and directives to align legal frameworks and promote safe, trustworthy AI deployment.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in exams and qualifications, aiming to keep them fair and trustworthy. The document sets rules and checks to prevent cheating, protect students’ privacy, and ensure AI tools don’t compromise the reliability of assessment results.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how AI systems use copyrighted material, analyzing legal implications, risks, and potential benefits for creators and developers. It outlines recommendations for policy changes and best practices to balance innovation with intellectual property protection.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued its official response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on artificial intelligence, titled “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” The response outlines the government’s plans to strengthen regulation, boost research and development, and address ethical and safety concerns to ensure AI benefits society while mitigating risks.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the purpose, scope and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence relates to public standards. It also includes a FAQ section that addresses common questions about the committee’s work and AI’s impact on public standards.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee on the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission outlines the challenges, opportunities, and recommended policy actions for effective AI governance.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy examines how artificial intelligence will influence the regulation of medical products and outlines new guidelines to ensure safety and efficacy. It adopts the principles from the AI White Paper to guide regulatory changes and promote responsible AI use in medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organization the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑driven defence body in the world for its size. It focuses on using AI to improve operational capabilities, build confidence, and lead in defence technology.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan is a framework by the Department for Transport that aims to work with the transport sector to tap into the benefits of AI while carefully managing any risks that could arise. It outlines strategies, partnerships, and safeguards to promote responsible, safe, and effective use of AI in transportation.
